question.:question/problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $A$ into the matrix $B$, where

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -11 & 0 & 2 \\ 10 & 5 & -5\end{bmatrix}
$$

$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -11 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}?
$$

First, notice that the $1$st and $2$nd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $3$rd row.

By considering the given row operations that modify the $3$rd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -11 & 0 & 2 \\ 10 & 5 & -5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\ & \sim\begin{bmatrix}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -11 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\ & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1}.
$$

X=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 9 & 0 \\ 4 & 9 & -5 \\ 2 & -8 & 6\end{bmatrix},\,Y=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 9 & 0 \\ 4 & 9 & -5 \\ -4 & 16 & -12\end{bmatrix}?
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd and the $1$st rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $3$rd row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $3$rd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 9 & 0 \\ 4 & 9 & -5 \\ 2 & -8 & 6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3}:=(-2)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 9 & 0 \\ 4 & 9 & -5 \\ -4 & 16 & -12\end{bmatrix} \\  & =Y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:=(-2)\cdot {R}_{3}.
$$
